digest.component_or_area: test infrastructure: subprocess timeout and network stall sentinels
propositions: Five real-subprocess reap tests burn ~1s wall-clock each waiting for a shared 1s autouse timeout fixture to expire, creating a latent load flake
A concurrent test (test_run_acli_429_retries_with_rate_limit_backoff) must complete two spawns within the same 1s ceiling, creating a latent load flake in the opposite direction

Three reap tests assert on child-side setup (grandchild pidfile, spawn counter, flushed stdout) but rely on implicit ordering via the injected window being larger than interpreter startup, not explicit synchronization
The tight_stall fixture injects a 2s low-speed window when a sibling test already proved git honors 1s, wasting test time

Splitting and shrinking per-test timeout windows, adding explicit readiness gates for setup ordering, and reducing injected stall windows maintains sentinel discrimination while eliminating wall-clock coupling
